# Revenues, GDP and welfare {#sec-fiscal}

This chapter follows the money. Once the model knows how much of each fuel is used and how much electricity is
generated in a year, it can say what the government collects and what it pays out, how spending that revenue moves
GDP, how the energy import bill changes, how heavily carbon is priced in effect, and what the policy is worth to
society once climate damages, air pollution, road externalities and efficiency costs are counted.

The blocks of the chapter, in the order the model computes them within a year:

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  A["Fuel use, power"] --> R["Revenues<br/>by fuel, sector, instrument"]
  R --> C["Carbon pricing<br/>indicators"]
  R --> F["Fiscal space,<br/>impulse, GDP effect"]
  F -- "next year" --> G["GDP level and growth"]
  G --> A
  A --> X["External balance"]
  A --> W["Welfare and<br/>externalities"]
  E["Emissions"] --> W
  E --> C
```

The GDP effect of a year acts on GDP only in the following year. That one-year lag is the only link from year $t$ to
year $t+1$ in this chapter, and it is what keeps the model free of circular references (@sec-fi-timing).

**Notation.** Every equation holds for each scenario $o$ and country $c$; these indices are omitted. The year $t$ is
shown only where an equation reaches into another year. A superscript $B$ marks the value of the baseline (scenario 1)
in the same year, and $\Delta x = x - x^{B}$. Subsector $s$, sector group $g$ (transport, buildings, industry, other
energy use, power) and fuel $f$ follow @sec-model-overview. Equation ids in brackets, such as
([M6.1](A_Equations.qmd#eqlist-M6-1)), point to the equation list.

| Symbol | Meaning | Unit or value |
|---|---|---|
| $\theta$ | PJ per ktoe (`PJ per ktoe`) | fuel use in ktoe times $\theta$ times USD/GJ gives USD million |
| $F_{s,f}$ | fuel use of fuel $f$ in subsector $s$ (`ener`) | ktoe |
| $Y^{0}$ | baseline real GDP (`gdp.usd`) | USD bn |
| $M$ | million per billion (`MperBn`) | 1000 |
| money | real USD of the results year | USD million for revenues, USD bn for GDP, trade and welfare |

## Header and summary rows {#sec-fi-header}

A handful of macro rows sit at the top of every scenario: they give the GDP against which revenues, trade and welfare
are scaled. Every section of the model also ends with a summary row, so the results can be read at a glance.

### GDP rows of the header {#sec-fi-header-gdp}

Baseline real GDP comes from the IMF World Economic Outlook, extended past its last data year as described in
([M0.1](A_Equations.qmd#eqlist-M0-1)). The exchange rate is the one implied by real GDP in the two currencies, so it is
constant in real terms:

$$
e = \frac{Y^{LCU}}{Y^{0}}
$$ {#eq-fi-xr}

where

- $Y^{LCU}$ is baseline real GDP in local currency (`gdp.lcu`), bn;
- $Y^{0}$ is baseline real GDP in USD (`gdp.usd`), bn;
- $e$ is the exchange rate (`xr`), local currency per USD (Egypt: 14.34 EGP per USD).

| Code | Content | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `gdp.usd` | Real GDP, baseline, USD bn | WEO; every "% of GDP" row of this chapter divides by it |
| `gdp.lcu` | Real GDP, baseline, local currency bn | WEO |
| `xr` | Exchange rate implied by real GDP (@eq-fi-xr) | computed |
| `gdp.pos.pct` | Real GDP growth after the GDP feedback (@eq-fi-growth) | computed; the summary row of the header |
| `gdpn.lcu`, `gdpn.usd` | Nominal GDP in local currency and in USD, bn | WEO `NGDP` and `NGDPD`, extended with the last nominal growth rate |

Baseline real GDP is data, not a model result, so dividing by it never creates a circular reference.

### Summary rows {#sec-fi-summary}

Every section of the model ends with its summary row: the one row shown when the section is rolled up. Four sections
have a second summary row, the change against the baseline. Sub-blocks (11b, 12d, 13b, 14b, 16b) sit inside their
section, before its notes and summary.

| Section | Summary row | Change against the baseline |
|---|---|---|
| 0 Header | `gdp.pos.pct` real GDP growth after the feedback | |
| 2 Prices | `rpe` average retail energy price, all energy (USD/GJ) | |
| 11 Energy use | total energy use | `echg.all` |
| 12 Revenues | `rtot` total revenue | `rtot.chg` |
| 13 CO2 | energy CO2 | `co2.chg` |
| 14 GHGs | total GHG emissions | `ghg.chg` |
| 17 Carbon pricing | `ecr` effective carbon rate | |
| 18 Welfare | `wel.usd` national welfare gain | |

Every "change against the baseline" reads scenario 1 in the same year only. The lookup stops at the current year, so
it can never reach a later year of scenario 1 (@sec-fi-timing).

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="In Excel-AI and CPAT Python"}
- **Excel-AI:** sheet Mitigation, section 0 (rows 11-14: `gdp.usd`, `gdp.lcu`, `xr`, `gdp.pos.pct`; rows 1-5 hold the
  years, title, band, scenario name and number and are frozen); `gdpn` in section 12. The baseline value of the same
  year is read through helper row 10 (`INDEX` of scenario 1 up to this column at the position of this year).
- **CPAT Python:** `cpat_model/mitigation/header.py`, `prepare()` (equations M0.1, M0.2); the baseline value of the same
  year is `totals.reference()`.
:::

## Revenues {#sec-fi-revenues}

Revenue is computed fuel by fuel and subsector by subsector: fuel use times a tax, subsidy or policy rate per GJ. The
model keeps three separate lines (existing taxes, existing subsidies, new policies), adds the power sector, subsidy
reforms, producer subsidies and the methane fee, and then rearranges the same money by fuel and by policy instrument.
The methodology describes this in
[section 3.6, Fiscal revenues](../CPAT_full_documentation_html/03_Mitigation.html#fiscal-revenues).

All revenue rows are in USD million, real. A negative number is a fiscal cost (a subsidy).

### Revenue of each fuel and subsector {#sec-fi-rev-pair}

For each subsector $s$ and fuel $f$, the price block of the fuel (@sec-prices) gives the components of the retail
price per GJ. Revenue multiplies them by fuel use.

**Existing taxes** include excise and other taxes, the VAT payment, and the change in existing carbon pricing against
the year embedded in the price data, with VAT on that change
([M6.2](A_Equations.qmd#eqlist-M6-2)):

$$
revExi_{s,f} = \theta\,F_{s,f}\left(txo^{+}_{c} + vat_{c} + \Delta xcp_{s,f}\,(1 + v_{s,f})\right)
$$ {#eq-fi-rtx}

**Existing consumer subsidies** are the negative part of the existing taxes:

$$
cs_{s,f} = \theta\,F_{s,f}\,txo^{-}_{c}
$$ {#eq-fi-rsub}

**New policies** are the new carbon tax, the new excise (fuel price reform, and Pigouvian taxes where they are switched
on), the ETS cost on the auctioned part, and VAT on all of them ([M6.1](A_Equations.qmd#eqlist-M6-1)):

$$
rev^{new}_{s,f} = \theta\,F_{s,f}\left(nct_{s,f} + nexc_{s,f} + \rho\,nets_{s,f} + v_{s,f}\,nce_{s,f}\right)
$$ {#eq-fi-rnew}

**Subsidy reform** removes consumer subsidies and price controls as separate policy lines; its revenue includes VAT:

$$
rev^{sr}_{s,f} = \theta\,F_{s,f}\,(csw_{s,f} + pcw_{s,f})\,(1 + v_{s,f})
$$ {#eq-fi-rsr}

where

- $c = c(s,f)$ is the price fuel of the pair (its price position in the price blocks);
- $txo^{+}_{c}$, $txo^{-}_{c}$ are the positive part (taxes, `etx`) and negative part (subsidies, `esub`) of excise and
  other taxes, USD/GJ;
- $vat_{c}$ is the VAT payment on the price before new policies (`vat`), USD/GJ;
- $\Delta xcp_{s,f}$ is the change in existing carbon pricing against the price data (`xcpd`), USD/GJ;
- $v_{s,f}$ is the VAT rate of the pair (Inputs), share;
- $nct$, $nexc$, $nets$ are the new carbon tax (`ctxnew`), new excise (`ntx`) and ETS cost (`ets`), USD/GJ, and
  $nce$ their total (`nce`);
- $\rho$ is the ETS revenue factor, the auctioned share (`ets.rf`); feebates are revenue-neutral and raise nothing;
- $csw$, $pcw$ are the consumer subsidy reform wedge and the price-control phase-out wedge of the subsector
  (`csw`, `pcw`; @sec-prices), USD/GJ.

Two splits of the same money are kept per pair for the report by instrument (@sec-fi-reports): the new excise and the
VAT.

$$
rev^{exc}_{s,f} = \theta\,F_{s,f}\,nexc_{s,f}, \qquad
rev^{vat}_{s,f} = \theta\,F_{s,f}\left(vat_{c} + (\Delta xcp_{s,f} + nce_{s,f} + csw_{s,f} + pcw_{s,f})\,v_{s,f}\right)
$$ {#eq-fi-rex}

A memo row gives the level of existing carbon pricing, $rev^{xcp}_{s,f} = \theta\,F_{s,f}\,xcp_{s,f}$ (`rxcp`). Only
its change against the price data is revenue (inside @eq-fi-rtx); the part embedded in the price data is already in
the excise.

| Row | Content | Equation |
|---|---|---|
| `rtx` | Existing taxes (excise and other taxes, VAT, change in existing carbon pricing) | @eq-fi-rtx |
| `rsub` | Existing consumer subsidies (negative) | @eq-fi-rsub |
| `rnew` | New policies (carbon tax, excise, auctioned ETS, VAT on them) | @eq-fi-rnew |
| `rsr` | Subsidy reform (consumer subsidy and price-control phase-outs, VAT included) | @eq-fi-rsr |
| `rex`, `rvt` | New excise; VAT (parts of the rows above, for the report by instrument) | @eq-fi-rex |
| `rxcp` | Existing carbon pricing, level (memo) | |

::: {.callout-tip icon=false title="Pseudocode: revenue of each fuel and subsector"}
```
for t in years:
    for s in subsectors:
        for f in fuels:
            c = price_fuel[f, s]; q = ener[f, s, t] * PJ_PER_KTOE
            v = vat_rate[f, s]
            rtx[f, s, t]  = q * (etx[c, t] + vat[c, t] + xcpd[f, s, t] * (1 + v))
            rsub[f, s, t] = q * esub[c, t]                               # negative
            rnew[f, s, t] = q * (ctxnew[f, s, t] + ntx[f, s, t]
                                 + ets[f, s, t] * ets_rf[t] + nce[f, s, t] * v)
            rsr[f, s, t]  = q * (csw[f, s, t] + pcw[f, s, t]) * (1 + v)
            rex[f, s, t]  = q * ntx[f, s, t]
            wedge = xcpd[f, s, t] + nce[f, s, t] + csw[f, s, t] + pcw[f, s, t]
            rvt[f, s, t]  = q * (vat[c, t] + wedge * v)
            rxcp[f, s, t] = q * xcp[f, s, t]                             # memo
```
:::

### Power-sector revenues {#sec-fi-rev-power}

The power sector raises revenue in two places: on the fuels burnt in power plants, and on the electricity sold to
users. Both are computed in the power block (@sec-power) and summed here
([A6.1](A_Equations.qmd#eqlist-A6-1)).

**By generation type $k$** (coal, gas, oil, nuclear, wind, solar, hydro, other renewables, biomass):

$$
\begin{aligned}
rev^{tx}_{k}  &= \delta_k\,\theta\,PE_k\,(txo^{+} + vat)_{c(k)} && \text{existing fuel taxes }(\texttt{prtx})\\
rev^{sub}_{k} &= \delta_k\,\theta\,PE_k\,txo^{-}_{c(k)} && \text{existing fuel subsidies }(\texttt{prsub})\\
rev^{xc}_{k}  &= xc_k\,H\,G_k && \text{change in existing carbon pricing }(\texttt{prxc})\\
rev^{new}_{k} &= pc_k\,H\,G_k - CO2_k\,A_{pow}\,(1 - \rho) && \text{new policies }(\texttt{prnew})\\
rev^{rns}_{k} &= rns_k\,H\,G_k && \text{renewable subsidies }(\texttt{prrns}\text{, negative})
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-fi-prev}

where

- $\delta_k$ is 1 for a type that burns a fuel (coal, gas, oil, biomass), else 0;
- $PE_k$ is the fuel use of type $k$ (`pe`), ktoe, and $c(k)$ its price fuel;
- $G_k$ is generation (`gen_mwy`), MW-years, and $H$ converts MW-years to million kWh (`MWyMkWh`, 8.76);
- $xc_k$, $pc_k$ are the existing carbon cost and the new policy cost per kWh of the type (`xck`, `xac`), USD/kWh;
- $CO2_k$ is the CO2 of the type, MtCO2, and $A_{pow}$ the ETS cost rate of power (`etr`), USD/tCO2: the free part of
  the ETS, $1-\rho$, is not revenue, so the ETS counts at the permit price on the auctioned part only;
- $rns_k$ is the renewable subsidy per kWh (`rns`), USD/kWh.

A memo row gives the level of existing carbon pricing of each type, `prxl` = $CO2_k$ times the existing carbon tax and
ETS prices of the price data year.

**By electricity user group $u$** (residential, industry):

$$
\begin{aligned}
rev^{vat}_{u}  &= pp_u\,\frac{v_u}{1+v_u}\,cons_u && \text{VAT on electricity }(\texttt{rvat})\\
rev^{nvat}_{u} &= \left(\overline{pc}\,\pi\,(1 - rb) + x_u\right) v_u\,cons_u && \text{VAT on the policy cost passed through }(\texttt{rnvat})\\
rev^{reb}_{u}  &= -\,rb\,\overline{pc}\,\pi\,cons_u && \text{rebate of the carbon cost }(\texttt{rreb}\text{, negative})\\
rev^{x}_{u}    &= x_u\,cons_u && \text{electricity excise }(\texttt{rpex})\\
rev^{gap}_{u}  &= gap_u\,cons_u && \text{electricity subsidy gap }(\texttt{rgap}\text{, negative})
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-fi-uelec}

where $pp_u$ is the electricity price before policies (`rppre`), $\overline{pc}$ the average policy cost of
generation (`ccpav`), $\pi$ the pass-through of the power-sector price change (`PowerSectorPriceChangePassOn`),
$rb$ the rebate switch (`rbs`), $x_u$ the electricity excise (`pex`), $gap_u$ the subsidy gap (`sgap`), all per kWh,
$v_u$ the VAT rate and $cons_u$ consumption in million kWh. The excise splits into the excise of the scenario
"Electricity excise" (`rexs` = `exs` times total consumption) and the manual excise (`rexm`, the rest).

The power sector's lines of the three revenue totals are then:

$$
\begin{aligned}
rev^{tx}_{pow}  &= \textstyle\sum_k (rev^{tx}_{k} + rev^{xc}_{k}) + \sum_u rev^{vat}_{u}\\
rev^{sub}_{pow} &= \textstyle\sum_k (rev^{sub}_{k} + rev^{rns}_{k}) + \sum_u rev^{gap}_{u}\\
rev^{new}_{pow} &= \textstyle\sum_k rev^{new}_{k} + \sum_u (rev^{nvat}_{u} + rev^{reb}_{u} + rev^{x}_{u})
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-fi-powtot}

Subsidy reform raises nothing in power (`rsr.pow` = 0).

### Producer subsidies and the methane fee {#sec-fi-rev-other}

**Producer subsidies** are a fiscal cost outside the fuel and subsector pairs. For each fuel group $f$ (coal, gas, oil,
biomass, electricity), the subsidy before any phase-out is scaled by the phase-out factor:

$$
rev^{psu} = -\sum_{f} pros_f\,psf_f, \qquad psf_f = 1 - \psi_f\,(1 - pof)
$$ {#eq-fi-rpsu}

where

- $pros_f$ is the producer subsidy before the phase-out (`pros`), USD million: price data (USD bn nominal) times the
  CPI factor up to the last price year, then held;
- $\psi_f$ is the inclusion switch of the fuel and $pof$ the phase-out factor of producer subsidies (@sec-prices);
- $psf_f$ is the share that remains (`psf`).

The phase-out also lowers the supply cost and so the prices (@sec-prices); this row is its fiscal line (`rpsu`).

**The methane fee** raises $rev^{mf}$ (`rmf` = `ch4.rev`): methane emissions of the sources the fee covers, times their
global warming potential, times the fee. It is computed with the methane block (@sec-emissions). It is not a fuel
revenue, so it appears in the totals and in the report by instrument, not in the report by fuel.

### Totals {#sec-fi-rev-totals}

The totals add the pairs over subsectors and fuels and add the power line. Net revenue from existing taxes and
subsidies, and total revenue ([M6.3](A_Equations.qmd#eqlist-M6-3)):

$$
rev^{net} = \sum_{s,f} (revExi_{s,f} + cs_{s,f}) + rev^{tx}_{pow} + rev^{sub}_{pow}
$$ {#eq-fi-rnet}

$$
rev = rev^{net} + rev^{new} + rev^{sr} + rev^{psu} + rev^{mf}
$$ {#eq-fi-rtot}

$$
\Delta rev = rev - rev^{B}
$$ {#eq-fi-rchg}

where $rev^{new} = \sum_{s,f} rev^{new}_{s,f} + rev^{new}_{pow}$ and $rev^{sr} = \sum_{s,f} rev^{sr}_{s,f}$. The lines
`rtx`, `rsub`, `rnew`, `rxcp` and `rsr` are also summed by sector group (transport, buildings, industry, other energy
use) and given for power.

| Row | Content | Unit |
|---|---|---|
| `rnet` | Net revenue from existing taxes and subsidies (@eq-fi-rnet) | USD m |
| `rtot` | Total revenue (@eq-fi-rtot); summary row of section 12 | USD m |
| `rtot.ref` | Total revenue of scenario 1, same year | USD m |
| `rtot.chg` | Change in total revenue against scenario 1 (@eq-fi-rchg); second summary row | USD m |
| `rev.chk` | Check: totals of `rtx`, `rsub`, `rnew` minus the sum of their sector and power rows (0) | USD m |

::: {.callout-tip icon=false title="Pseudocode: revenue totals"}
```
for t in years:
    power = {
        'rtx':  sum(prtx[k, t] + prxc[k, t] for k in types)
                + sum(rvat[u, t] for u in users),
        'rsub': sum(prsub[k, t] + prrns[k, t] for k in types)
                + sum(rgap[u, t] for u in users),
        'rnew': sum(prnew[k, t] for k in types)
                + sum(rnvat[u, t] + rreb[u, t] + rpex[u, t] for u in users),
        'rxcp': sum(prxl[k, t] for k in types),
        'rsr':  0.0,
    }
    for var in ['rtx', 'rsub', 'rnew', 'rxcp', 'rsr']:
        for g in groups:                                  # tra, bld, ind, oen
            var[g, t] = sum(var[f, s, t] for s in subsectors_of(g) for f in fuels)
        var['pow', t] = power[var]
        var['all', t] = sum(var[f, s, t] for s in subsectors for f in fuels) \
                        + power[var]
    rmf[t]  = ch4_rev[t]
    rpsu[t] = -sum(pros[f, t] * psf[f, t] for f in ['coa', 'nga', 'oil', 'bio', 'ecy'])
    rnet[t] = rtx['all', t] + rsub['all', t]
    rtot[t] = rnet[t] + rnew['all', t] + rsr['all', t] + rpsu[t] + rmf[t]
    rtot_chg[t] = rtot[t] - baseline.rtot[t]              # scenario 1, same year
```
:::

### Fiscal reports {#sec-fi-reports}

The fiscal reports (block 12d) rearrange the same revenue three ways: by fuel, by policy instrument, and against GDP.
Each report has a check row that must be 0, because it splits the totals exactly.

**Revenue by fuel, net of subsidies.** For each final-use fuel, the existing taxes, subsidies, new policies and subsidy
reform over all subsectors. Electricity collects its VAT, subsidy gap, VAT on the policy cost, rebates, excise and
renewable subsidies. Fuels burnt in power plants have their own rows:

$$
rfu_{f} = \sum_{s} \left(revExi_{s,f} + cs_{s,f} + rev^{new}_{s,f} + rev^{sr}_{s,f}\right), \qquad
rfu_{ecy} = \sum_u \left(rev^{vat}_u + rev^{nvat}_u + rev^{reb}_u + rev^{x}_u + rev^{gap}_u\right) + \sum_k rev^{rns}_k
$$ {#eq-fi-rfu}

$$
rfg_{k} = rev^{tx}_{k} + rev^{xc}_{k} + rev^{sub}_{k} + rev^{new}_{k}, \qquad k \in \{\text{coal, gas, oil, biomass}\}
$$ {#eq-fi-rfg}

The check `rfu.chk` = $\left|\sum_f rfu_f + rfu_{ecy} + \sum_k rfg_k - rev^{net} - rev^{new} - rev^{sr}\right|$ is 0.
The methane fee and producer subsidies are not fuel revenues and are not in these rows.

**Total revenue by policy instrument** (block 12e, [A6.2](A_Equations.qmd#eqlist-A6-2)). The same total, split by the
instrument that raises it:

| Row | Instrument | Definition |
|---|---|---|
| `rpol.ct` | New carbon tax | $\sum_e CO2^{cov}_e\,ct_e$ over the 17 coverage sectors $e$ (power included) + electricity rebates `rreb` + electricity excise of the scenario `rexs` |
| `rpol.ets` | Auctioned ETS | $\rho \sum_e CO2_e\,etr_e$ |
| `rpol.exc` | New excise (fuel price reform) | $\sum_{s,f} rev^{exc}_{s,f} + \sum_k rev^{new}_k$ − `rpol.ctp` − `rpol.etp` + manual electricity excise `rexm` |
| `rpol.vat` | VAT | $\sum_{s,f} rev^{vat}_{s,f} + \sum_u (rev^{vat}_u + rev^{nvat}_u)$ |
| `rpol.psu` | Producer subsidies | electricity subsidy gap $\sum_u rev^{gap}_u$ + $rev^{psu}$ |
| `rpol.ren` | Renewable subsidies | $\sum_k rev^{rns}_k$ |
| `rpol.mf` | Methane fee | $rev^{mf}$ |
| `rpol.trs` | Transport revenues | 0 (not modelled) |
| `rpol.exi` | Existing taxes and subsidies | the remainder: $rev$ − `rpol.mf` − `ct` − `exc` − `vat` − `ets` − `psu` − `ren` |
| `rpol.tot` | Total | sum of the rows above; equals $rev$ (check `rpol.chk` = 0) |
| `rpol.ctp`, `rpol.etp` | Of which power: carbon tax, ETS | $CO2^{cov}_{pow}\,ct_{pow}$; $CO2_{pow}\,etr_{pow}\,\rho$ (memo, not in the total) |

Here $CO2^{cov}_e$ is the CO2 covered by the new carbon tax in sector $e$ (`covct`, @eq-fi-covct), $ct_e$ the
sector's carbon tax rate (`ctr`), $CO2_e$ the sector's CO2 (`co2.sec`) and $etr_e$ its ETS cost rate. "Existing taxes
and subsidies" is the remainder: fuel use times excise and the change in existing carbon pricing, consumer subsidies,
subsidy reform, and the taxes and subsidies on power fuels.

**Base erosion and shares of GDP.** A policy that lowers fuel use also changes what the existing taxes raise and what
the existing subsidies cost. Base erosion measures that change:

$$
rbe = rev^{net} - rev^{net,B}
$$ {#eq-fi-rbe}

Each total is also given as a share of baseline real GDP:

$$
rpct_{x} = \frac{x}{Y^{0}\,M}, \qquad x \in \{rev,\ rev^{net},\ rev^{sub},\ rev^{new},\ \Delta rev,\ rbe\}
$$ {#eq-fi-rpct}

| Row | Content |
|---|---|
| `rfu.<fuel>`, `rfu.ecy` | Revenue by final-use fuel and electricity, net of subsidies (@eq-fi-rfu) |
| `rfg.<type>` | Revenue from fuels burnt in power generation (@eq-fi-rfg) |
| `rfu.chk` | Check of the report by fuel (0) |
| `rpol.<instrument>` | Total revenue by policy instrument (table above); `rpol.chk` its check (0) |
| `rbe` | Base erosion (@eq-fi-rbe) |
| `rpct.tot`, `.net`, `.sub`, `.new`, `.chg`, `.be` | Total, net existing, subsidies, new policies, change against scenario 1, base erosion, as shares of GDP (@eq-fi-rpct) |

::: {.callout-tip icon=false title="Pseudocode: fiscal reports"}
```
for t in years:
    for f in fuels:
        rfu[f, t] = sum(rtx[f, s, t] + rsub[f, s, t] + rnew[f, s, t] + rsr[f, s, t]
                        for s in subsectors)
    rfu['ecy', t] = sum(rvat[u, t] + rnvat[u, t] + rreb[u, t] + rpex[u, t] + rgap[u, t]
                        for u in users) + sum(prrns[k, t] for k in types)
    for k in ['coa', 'nga', 'oop', 'bio']:
        rfg[k, t] = prtx[k, t] + prxc[k, t] + prsub[k, t] + prnew[k, t]

    for e in coverage_sectors:                       # 17: power and the 16 subsectors
        fuels_e = ['coa', 'nga', 'oop'] if e == 'pow' else fuels
        covct[e, t] = sum(co2[f, e, t] * ctcov[f, t] for f in fuels_e) * (ctr[e, t] > 0)
    ctp = covct['pow', t] * ctr['pow', t]
    etp = co2_sec['pow', t] * etr['pow', t] * ets_rf[t]
    rpol['ct']  = sum(covct[e, t] * ctr[e, t] for e in coverage_sectors) \
                  + sum(rreb[u, t] for u in users) + rexs[t]
    rpol['exc'] = sum(rex[f, s, t]) + sum(prnew[k, t]) - ctp - etp + rexm[t]
    rpol['vat'] = sum(rvt[f, s, t]) + sum(rvat[u, t] + rnvat[u, t] for u in users)
    rpol['ets'] = sum(co2_sec[e, t] * etr[e, t] for e in coverage_sectors) * ets_rf[t]
    rpol['psu'] = sum(rgap[u, t] for u in users) + rpsu[t]
    rpol['ren'] = sum(prrns[k, t] for k in types)
    rpol['mf'], rpol['trs'] = rmf[t], 0.0
    rpol['exi'] = rtot[t] - rmf[t] - rpol['ct'] - rpol['exc'] - rpol['vat'] \
                  - rpol['ets'] - rpol['psu'] - rpol['ren']

    rbe[t] = rnet[t] - baseline.rnet[t]
    for key, x in [('tot', rtot), ('net', rnet), ('sub', rsub['all']),
                   ('new', rnew['all']), ('chg', rtot_chg), ('be', rbe)]:
        rpct[key, t] = x[t] / (gdp_usd[t] * M_PER_BN)
```
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="In Excel-AI and CPAT Python"}
- **Excel-AI:** the pair rows `rtx`, `rsub`, `rnew`, `rxcp`, `rsr`, `rex`, `rvt` sit in every subsector block of
  sections 5-8; the power rows `prtx` ... `prrns` in section 3 (block M) and `rvat` ... `rgap` in section 3 (block G);
  `pros`, `psf` in section 2. Sheet Mitigation, section 12: the totals (`rmf`, `rpsu`, `rnet`, `rtot`, `rtot.ref`,
  `rtot.chg`, `rev.chk`), block 12d (`rfu`, `rfg`, `rfu.chk`, `rbe`, `rpct`, `gdpn`) and block 12e (`rpol`,
  `rpol.chk`). Sums over subsectors use `SUMIFS` on the block columns `SecVar` and `SecFuel`; shares of GDP call the
  LAMBDA `GDPSHARE` in the LAMBDA column.
- **CPAT Python:** the pair rows in `cpat_model/mitigation/fuel_use.py`, `step()`; the power rows in
  `cpat_model/mitigation/power.py`, `step()`; totals and reports in `cpat_model/mitigation/totals.py`, `revenues()`
  (equations M6.1-M6.3, A6.1, A6.2).
:::

::: {.callout-warning collapse="true" title="Differences from legacy CPAT"}
- **Revenue structure (LD37), as legacy:** the three calculations per subsector and fuel (existing taxes with VAT,
  consumer subsidies, new policies), power as before, plus block 12e, total revenue by policy as legacy rows
  8016-8027. Legacy bugs L70 (industry gas excise uses the coal rate and coal use), L71 (biomass taxes, subsidies and
  VAT divided by the unit conversion), L72 (next-year references), L73 (wrong coverage shares) and L75 (revenue reports:
  hard-coded row and mixed totals) do not arise: each pair takes its own rates, use and coverage.
- **Subsidy and price-control phase-outs (LD18):** separate policy lines as in legacy, with their revenue `rsr`.
- **Producer subsidies (LD19):** in the supply cost as in legacy, with the fiscal line `rpsu` by fuel.
- **Power:** the ETS revenue of power is valued at the permit price on the auctioned part (prototype bug M6 fixed); VAT
  on the policy term of electricity is included (M2 fixed); the renewable subsidy counts the base subsidy once (legacy
  bug L108 fixed).
- **Transport revenues** (`rpol.trs`) are 0: the vehicle revenues of the road engineer model are not modelled (issue
  I46).
- **Not built.** Revenue lost to price controls (the methodology's memo,
  [section 3.6.4.1](../CPAT_full_documentation_html/03_Mitigation.html#revenueslosses-from-price-controls)): legacy
  holds only pass-through coefficients (rows 746-760, 2216-2220), not a revenue row. Total fuel expenditures
  ([section 3.6.4.2](../CPAT_full_documentation_html/03_Mitigation.html#total-fuel-expenditures)) are the spending
  rows of the price memo (`pav.sp`, @sec-prices) and are not repeated here.
- **Methodology.** The methodology's revenue from existing taxes and VAT leaves out the other energy use sector and
  treats existing ETS permits differently when the existing ETS is the EU ETS
  ([section 3.6.3](../CPAT_full_documentation_html/03_Mitigation.html#total-revenues-raised-by-policy)). The model
  follows legacy's revenue rows: each pair takes its own price components, and existing carbon pricing enters through
